events.title: William the Conqueror Lands in England
events.description: William, Duke of Normandy, landed with a large invasion fleet at Pevensey on the Sussex coast. This began the Norman conquest of England.
events.significance: The conquest transformed English government, language, landholding and culture, and its effects shaped England for centuries.

events.title: Cabrillo Reaches the California Coast
events.description: Navigator Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo sailed into the bay at what is now San Diego. He was the first European to explore the coast of present-day California.
events.significance: His voyage opened the Pacific coast of North America to European exploration and mapping.

events.title: The Siege of Yorktown Begins
events.description: American forces, backed by a French fleet and French troops, began the siege of the British army at Yorktown, Virginia.
events.significance: The siege was the last major battle of the American Revolutionary War and ended in the British surrender weeks later.

events.title: Fleming Notices the Mold That Led to Penicillin
events.description: Alexander Fleming noticed a mold in his London laboratory that was killing the bacteria around it. The mold later became known as penicillin.
events.significance: Penicillin became the first widely used antibiotic and has saved countless lives.

events.title: Warsaw Surrenders to Nazi Germany
events.description: After weeks of siege and bombardment, Warsaw surrendered to German forces. Germany and the Soviet Union then agreed on how to divide Poland between them.
events.significance: It marked the end of organized Polish resistance in the 1939 campaign and the start of a brutal occupation.
